title: Reported Speech & Voice for Boards
description: Board-focused reported speech and voice for Grade 10: mixed narration, voice in all tenses, exam patterns and common traps, with bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Mixed Narration
topics.concept:
A real dialogue mixes statements, questions and commands. To report it, apply the right move to each part and link them smoothly with reporting verbs (said, asked, replied, told, requested, exclaimed, added).

  • Statement → said/replied that + back-shifted clause.
  • Yes/No question → asked if/whether + statement order.
  • Wh- question → asked + wh- word + statement order.
  • Command/request → told/requested + (not) to + verb.
  • Exclamation/wish → exclaimed with joy/sorrow that / prayed that.

Remember the universal back-shift (is→was, will→would), pronoun changes, and time-word changes (now→then, today→that day). Don't back-shift universal truths.

examples.problem: Report: "Where are you going?" he asked. "To the market," she said.
examples.solution: He asked where she was going. She replied that she was going to the market.

examples.problem: Report: "Don't be late," mother said. "I won't," I promised.
examples.solution: Mother told me not to be late. I promised that I would not be (late).

recap: Apply the right move to each part: statement, question, command, exclamation
Link with reporting verbs: said, asked, replied, told, requested
Back-shift tenses, change pronouns and time words (but not universal truths)

topics.title: Voice in All Tenses & Board Patterns
topics.concept:
To change voice: move the object to the front, use the correct form of be in the same tense + the past participle, and put the old subject after 'by' (drop if unknown).

TensePassive form
Simple Presentis/are + V3
Present Continuousis/are being + V3
Present Perfecthas/have been + V3
Simple Pastwas/were + V3
Past Perfecthad been + V3
Future / Modalwill be / modal + be + V3

Board patterns: 'Change the voice', 'Rewrite as directed', 'Begin the sentence with the given word'. Watch traps: keep the tense, use the participle (not the past tense), and drop the object pronoun.

examples.problem: Change the voice: The gardener is watering the plants.
examples.solution: The plants are being watered by the gardener. — present continuous passive.

examples.problem: Change the voice: They had completed the work.
examples.solution: The work had been completed (by them). — past perfect passive.

recap: Passive = be (in the same tense) + past participle
Object → subject; old subject → by + agent (drop if unknown)
Traps: keep the tense, use V3, drop the object pronoun

questions.q: Report: 'She said, "I will come."'
options: She said that I would come.

questions.q: Voice of 'He is painting the wall':
Report: '"Do you like tea?" he asked.'
options: He asked if I liked tea.
He asked that I liked tea.
He asked do I like tea.
He asked if did I like tea.

questions.q: Voice of 'They cleaned the room':
Report: '"Don't run," he said.'
options: He told me not to run.
He told me to not running.
questions.explanation: Negative command → told + not to + verb.

questions.q: Voice of 'We have finished the project':
Report: 'He said, "I am reading."'
options: He said that I was reading.

questions.q: Voice of 'Someone broke the window':
Report: '"What is your name?" she asked.'
options: She asked what my name was.
She asked what was my name.
She asked that what my name was.
She asked what is my name.
questions.explanation: Wh- kept, no inversion, is → was.

questions.q: Voice (modal): 'You should respect elders.'
Report: 'She said, "The sun rises in the east."'
options: She said the sun rose in the east.
She said the sun rises in the east.
She said the sun had risen.
She said the sun will rise.

questions.q: Voice of 'They will build a bridge':
Report the mixed dialogue: 'He said, "I am leaving now, but I will return tomorrow."'
options: He said that he was leaving then but he would return the next day.
He said he is leaving now but will return tomorrow.
He said that he was leaving now but he will return tomorrow.
He told he was leaving and would return.

questions.q: Change the voice: 'People say that he is a fraud.'
options: It is said that he is a fraud.
He says he is a fraud.
It said he is a fraud.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'She asked me that whether I had finished.'
Change the voice: 'The teacher was explaining the lesson.'
options: The lesson was being explained by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive = was being + V3.

questions.q: Report the exclamation: 'He said, "Alas! I have failed."'
options: He exclaimed with sorrow that he had failed.
He said alas he had failed.
He asked if he had failed.
He told that he failed alas.
questions.explanation: Exclamation of sorrow → 'exclaimed with sorrow that …'.

questions.q: Change the voice of the double-object sentence: 'The principal gave him a prize.'
options: He was given a prize by the principal.
questions.explanation: The person object becomes the subject: 'He was given a prize …'.

questions.q: Report: 'She said to me, "Please help my brother."'
options: She requested me to help her brother.
She said me to help her brother.
She told to help her brother.
She asked me help her brother.
questions.explanation: Polite command → requested + object + to + verb; 'my' → 'her'.

questions.q: Change the voice: 'Has anyone solved the puzzle?'
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive question = Has … been + V3.

outcomes: Convert mixed passages between direct and indirect speech
Change voice across all tenses confidently
Handle special voice and narration cases
Recognise the exact board question patterns
Avoid the most common narration and voice traps

intro.en: Two transformation skills appear in almost every board paper: reported speech (narration) and voice. You have met both before; this chapter sharpens them for the exam — mixed dialogues, voice in all tenses, and the precise format examiners expect. These are reliable, scoring questions when your method is automatic.
intro.hi: लगभग हर बोर्ड पेपर में दो रूपांतरण-कौशल आते हैं: reported speech (narration) और voice। आप दोनों से पहले मिल चुके हैं; यह अध्याय इन्हें परीक्षा के लिए तेज़ करता है — मिश्रित संवाद, सभी tenses में voice, और वह सटीक format जो परीक्षक चाहते हैं। जब तरीका स्वतः हो जाए, ये भरोसेमंद, अंक देने वाले प्रश्न हैं।

real_life.situation:
A short dialogue to report:

Direct: "Have you finished?" the teacher asked. "Not yet," I replied.

Reported: The teacher asked whether I had finished. I replied that I had not finished yet.
real_life.why: A yes/no question became 'asked whether … had finished', and the short reply was expanded into a full reported statement. Boards love these mixed dialogues — knowing the moves lets you convert them fast and accurately.

rule_box.html:
SkillCore move
Narration: statementsaid that + back-shift
Narration: questionasked if/wh- + statement order
Narration: commandtold/asked + (not) to + verb
Voiceobject→subject, be(same tense)+V3, by+agent
rule_box.formula: Narration: back-shift + change pronouns/time · Voice: be + V3 in the same tense
rule_box.example: She said, "I wrote it." → She said that she had written it. (and passive: It had been written by her.)

quick_test.q: The present perfect 'has written' becomes which passive?
quick_test.explanation: Present perfect passive = has/have been + V3.

common_mistakes.wrong: He asked that where I was going.

common_mistakes.note: Use the past participle in the passive.

fill_l1.instructions: Give the passive of each active verb phrase (same tense).

items.answer: She said that she had done it.
He asked whether I was ready.
The road is being repaired (by them).
She told me to shut the door.

error_detection.sentence: He asked that what I wanted.
The work was do by them.
error_detection.correct: The work was done by them.

error_detection.sentence: She said she will help me.
error_detection.correct: She said she would help me.

sentence_correction.wrong: He told that he was busy.
sentence_correction.correct: He said that he was busy. (or: He told me that he was busy.)

sentence_correction.wrong: The house is build by them.
sentence_correction.correct: The house is built by them.

sentence_correction.wrong: She asked me where was I going.
sentence_correction.correct: She asked me where I was going.

rearrangement.jumbled: by / written / was / her / the / letter
rearrangement.answer: The letter was written by her.

rearrangement.jumbled: had / she / said / that / done / it / she
rearrangement.answer: She said that she had done it.

answers: has been written → present perfect passive
is being written → present continuous passive

reading.passage: "Have you completed the survey?" the officer asked. "Almost," the clerk replied, "but the forms are still being checked." "They must be submitted by Friday," the officer said firmly. "Don't delay." The clerk promised that everything would be ready on time, and the files were quickly sorted.

questions.q: Report the officer's question in indirect speech.
questions.answer: The officer asked whether the clerk had completed the survey.

questions.q: Identify a passive verb and name its tense.
questions.answer: 'are still being checked' (present continuous passive); 'must be submitted' (modal passive); 'were sorted' (past passive).

questions.q: Report the command 'Don't delay.'
questions.answer: The officer told the clerk not to delay.

speaking: She said that she had finished the work.
He asked whether I was coming.
The letters are being posted now.
The bridge was built last year.
She told me not to worry.

writing.prompt: Write a 4-line dialogue (a question, a reply, a command, a promise) in direct speech, then report all of it as one paragraph in indirect speech.
writing.example: Direct: "Will you help?" she asked. "Of course," I said. / Reported: She asked whether I would help. I replied that I would.

options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
A letter is written by her.

micro_quiz.q: Report: '"Where do you live?" he asked.'
options: He asked where do I live.
He asked that where I lived.
micro_quiz.explanation: Wh- word kept, no inversion, back-shifted.

micro_quiz.q: Voice of 'They have built a school':

options: She told me to sit down.

challenge.q: Change the voice: 'Who wrote this novel?'
options: By whom was this novel written?
challenge.explanation: Passive of a 'who' question with the agent: 'By whom was …?'

options: She said she saw him yesterday.
She said she had seen him the previous day.
She said she has seen him yesterday.
She said she sees him the day before.
challenge.explanation: Simple past → past perfect; 'yesterday' → 'the previous day'.

revision: Mixed narration: apply the right move to each part; link with reporting verbs
Back-shift tenses, change pronouns and time words (not universal truths)
Voice = be (same tense) + past participle; object → subject; old subject → by
Modal passive = modal + be + V3; impersonal passive = It is said that…
